hints: Notice e.m.f. has the same unit as potential difference, the volt $\text{V}$, so start from a relation such as $V = P/I$ or $V = W/Q$.
Recall power $P = W/t$ has base units $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$ and current $I$ already has base unit $\text{A}$.
Divide the base units of power by the base unit of current and check the powers of $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$ against the four options.
walkthrough: Identify that e.m.f. is energy per unit charge and is measured in volts, the same unit as potential difference $V$.
Use the governing relation $V = P/I$, where $P$ is power and $I$ is current.
Write power in SI base units: work $W = F \times d$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, then $P = W/t$ gives $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$.
Divide by current, whose SI base unit is $\text{A}$: $V = P/I$ gives $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$ divided by $\text{A}$, which is $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$.
Compare with the options: only the combination with $\text{m}^2$, $\text{s}^{-3}$ and $\text{A}^{-1}$ matches. This is option B.

options.A: This has $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$ and so is missing two divisions by time from power and energy.
options.B: Since $V = P/I$, with $P$ in $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$ and $I$ in $\text{A}$, this gives $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$.
options.C: This has $\text{A}$ instead of $\text{A}^{-1}$ and $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$, so current is multiplied rather than divided.
options.D: This has $\text{m}$ instead of $\text{m}^2$, so the energy part is missing one length-squared factor from work $F \times d$.
